primitives.name: SCoRE (Selective Conformal Risk Control)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model SCoRE (Selective Conformal Risk control with E-values): for each candidate test point, construct a *risk-adjusted e-value* E from the calibration data; select the point iff the e-value passes a threshold derived from the target risk level.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E': 'Risk-adjusted e-value (unitless, ≥ 0)', 'L': 'Bounded continuous loss (e.g., betting units, stake-normalized) with |L| ≤ B < ∞', 'α': 'Target mean deviation risk level (dimensionless, α ∈ [0,1])', 'ρ': 'Threshold derived from α and B'}
primitives.assumptions: Exchangeability of calibration and test data; boundedness of the loss; existence of a nonnegative e-value E satisfying E[L·E] ≤ 1, where L is the loss.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violations of the core condition E[L·E] ≤ 1 lead to inflated realized risk; heavy-tailed losses or misspecified e-values cause systematic over-selection.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, the e-value E maps to the reciprocal of a conformal p-value (E ∝ 1/p), and the threshold ρ corresponds to a betting fraction. The method transforms a sequence of independent bets into a supermartingale, providing a universal filter for selecting profitable wagers with finite-sample risk control.
layer2.telemetry: Walk-forward realized average loss per posted pick compared to nominal α; proportion of picks selected relative to baseline.

primitives.name: Mean Deviation Risk (MDR)
primitives.verbatim_quote: - MDR: E[L_ψ] (mean risk over the selection policy ψ); SDR: expected average risk over selected points.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_ψ': 'Realized loss on the subset selected by policy ψ (units)', 'ψ': 'Selection indicator function (binary)'}
primitives.assumptions: Bounded loss L; integrability of ψ; exchangeability of data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: MDR becomes undefined when the loss has infinite expectation, causing the risk controller to fail catastrophically on heavy-tailed distributions.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, MDR translates directly to the expected average betting unit per posted pick. Controlling MDR ensures that the long-term portfolio growth rate remains bounded, preventing ruin from excessive exposure to high-variance bets.
layer2.telemetry: Average realized units per pick, stratified by volatility decile.

primitives.name: Weighted SCoRE
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Weighted extension: under covariate shift, reweight the e-values by the likelihood ratio (density ratio between deployment and calibration covariates); validity carries over if the weights are correct.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'w(x) = \\frac{p_{\\text{deploy}}(x)}{p_{\\text{calib}}(x)}': 'Likelihood ratio (density ratio) of covariates x between deployment and calibration distributions (unitless)', 'E_w = w · E': 'Weighted e-value (≥ 0)', 'α_w': 'Target weighted mean deviation risk (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Correct specification of the density ratio w(x); exchangeability within both calibration and deployment data; bounded loss.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Incorrect weighting (ŵ ≠ w) causes the weighted e-value E_w to lose its supermartingale property, leading to invalid risk guarantees and potential over-selection in regions with mismatched covariate shifts.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, weighted SCoRE models regime changes such as season phases or market shifts by reweighting historical picks according to their relevance in the current environment. This allows the risk controller to adaptively calibrate thresholds without requiring complete retraining, preserving the finite-sample guarantee under time-varying covariate distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Drop in realized MDR when applying seasonal weights; increase in the number of picks retained after weighting.

reasoning_traces.think:
SCoRE generalizes the classical Neyman-Pearson lemma to selective prediction by treating the selection indicator ψ as a randomized test. The core condition E[L·E] ≤ 1 is a martingale requirement that ensures the expected loss on the selected set never exceeds the nominal threshold α. This duality between e-values and risk measures provides a clean separation: e-values quantify evidence against the null hypothesis of large loss, while risk measures specify the acceptable average loss. In GSE, this translates into a two-stage process: first, compute a conformal p-value (an e-value) from the model's predictive distribution; second, invert it to obtain a selection threshold that trades off power (number of picks) against risk control. The weighted extension handles covariate shift by importance sampling the martingale, ensuring that the risk guarantee holds even when the deployment distribution differs from the calibration data.
